utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. I was told that there's something that Mr. Tieger wants to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. I'll try to be brief. I debated whether or not to raise it at this point, but I thought doing so might save time over the long haul, and that's the matter of questions, linkage, and protective measures. The Court will recall that I raised that issue previously in private session, pointing to a couple of instances after or during the course of the first witness, in which the accused had made a link between protective measures and particular witnesses. It occurred again yesterday. I wanted to note a couple of the examples and strongly encourage the more rigorous application of attention to linkage between witnesses, protected information that may divulge -- or protected information that may divulge identities and questions that reveal protected information. One example occurred when the accused indicated that he would not mention the name of the village from which the person whose photograph and name he was about to publicly display came from, but as it turned out, he didn't mention the name, but the name of the boy is very well known. It's part of a notorious incident, rather a cause celeb known to many people, and certainly if not known to people, easily identified through a quick search of the web. So that's the kind of linkage that can be made. As the Presiding Judge indicated yesterday, there is easy expedience to avoid that problem. Another instance occurred when the accused said he didn't want a document displayed publicly, but then he read from the document. And immediately after reading from the document, including the name of a village, made the linkage by saying, So that person brought people from his village and your village, directly making the linkage. I want to underscore again the concern about the need to comply with protective measures and the need for significantly greater rigour in ensuring that the linkage between protected information and information divulged openly in court is not made. I think that would apply as well to any questions that are asked about why protective measures were sought or granted, that should be in private session. And I can't underscore more forcefully the need to be cautious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. I hope the accused, Mr. Karadzic, understood it as well, and then the Chamber will pay attention more robustly on the matter. Let us bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. While we're doing that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's one -- we've just discovered what we believe to be a disclosure violation with respect to the next witness, and I would wonder if this document that would be the subject of a motion, could be given to you before the witness comes in so that you could have looked at it, and so you'll know what we're talking about when we raise the issue. It's not in the e-court. It was just given to us as Rule 66(B) disclosure. But I could give you the number or I could ask the Prosecution to make it available, or I have a paper copy that can be copied. But it would be useful if you have that document, so that when the witness comes and we make a motion about that, you will know its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, it's not this immediate witness, it's the following witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, the following witness, Mr. Okun, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, might I be allowed to say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Robinson, you meant to say that you're going to file a motion in writing?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Actually, we were going to make an oral motion. We just saw the document today, and the witness is coming today, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I will hear you later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I agree that we should adhere to the protective measures granted, although we consider them to be superfluous and detrimental. But here the protective measures have been extended to include a whole area. I'm not allowed to mention any village where at least four drastic events took place. One village has almost 2.000 inhabitants. So why would a village disclose the identity of a person? And I'm afraid that the Prosecution is using protective measures to cast a shadow and cover a very important event that came before everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I do not accept your allegation that protective measures regime is superfluous and detrimental. Neither do I think that regime is that difficult for you to understand. So consult Mr. Robinson and design your examination in order not to violate the regime. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While we're waiting for the witness to come in, I didn't say the name. I just said, "your village," and the interpreter said the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, it is true, but if the village is to be identified together with the other circumstances, there may be situations that his identity may be revealed, so be very cautious, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we start again, I wonder, Mr. Robinson, could you be so kind as to provide the Chamber with the copies of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I could do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we begin today, then, I have some words to say to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, the Chamber understands that you have raised some concerns with the Victims and Witnesses Section about the manner in which you were treated during your evidence yesterday. In this regard, I would like to say a few words about this before we begin today. It is the nature of the legal process at this Tribunal that all witnesses are questioned both by the party who has called them and by the opposing party, in your situation being the accused Mr. Karadzic, who is entitled to do cross-examine you not in the capacity of an accused person, but in the capacity as Defence counsel for himself. I understand that that might be something that is difficult for you to understand, but that is a Rule of this Tribunal. When a witness enters the witness box to be cross-examined, he or she has to accept that he or she will be challenged, and sometimes with vigour. Therefore, often during such cross-examination, questions are put which are difficult or may be perceived to be impolite or improper by the witness being asked them. It is the Chamber's role and duty to prevent a witness from being harassed, insulted, or verbally abused during cross-examination, as well as to ensure that questions asked are relevant to the case. The Chamber will intervene in these circumstances, as we did yesterday on one occasion. Otherwise, as advised by my colleague Judge Baird yesterday, it is for you, the witness, to answer the questions put to you to the best of your ability and not for you to ask why such questions are being asked or to refuse to respond. We are sorry if you feel that you were unjustly treated yesterday. The Chamber was far from criticising you, but we merely wanted to provide you with guidance that seemed necessary. Please bear in mind that it is the accused, Mr. Karadzic, who is on trial here and who faces serious penalties if he's ultimately convicted of the charges against him. You are giving evidence that will assist the Chamber in making its final determination of those charges, and Mr. Karadzic is entitled to challenge your evidence as well as your own credibility. We are conscious of the fact that this can be an unpleasant experience for any witness, and we are grateful for your willingness to come to the Tribunal and go through this process yet again. The Chamber will do its utmost to ensure that you are asked questions in an appropriate manner, but again it is your duty, as a witness, to answer the questions put to you as concisely as you can. On this matter, the Chamber will not hear either from the witness or from the parties. We'll continue. I noted, Mr. Karadzic, you spent about an hour and 45 minutes yesterday -- I'm sorry, two hours and forty-four minutes in total. Given that you noted that you would need four hours in total, I would expect you to conclude your cross-examination by this -- during the course of this first session. Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I had hoped that if I get through 1995, that I will be given more time now, but anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm also concerned and worried that I didn't upset you in some way or insult you. That wasn't my intention at all. But I want to ask you: Did we know each other before the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I just saw you on the television screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, yesterday, on the last page, I think 110 of the transcript, you said that you were happy to come here to say what kind of man I am and to deal with me. Now, that is your right, but what I am asking you now is: Did somebody tell you that, or did you want to do that of your own accord?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody told me. It's your acts that speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you have the motive of dealing with me and settling accounts with me?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm just saying that the acts you committed speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry that you have that view. But, anyway, you said Elfeta Vaseli [phoen], the lady we talked about yesterday in connection with the child -- I'm sorry to hear that -- well, you said that she had -- that her family was killed. Her brother and father are still alive, but one brother was killed as a volunteer in the Croatian Army, and another was in the Muslim army, and she is hiding somewhere in the federation, but her brothers are living quite free; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well, actually, I don't know. I don't know anything about that. I don't think I ever saw the woman, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you don't know, so what you said, that she had a personal motive for doing what she did, is not true?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard people say that her family -- her entire family had been killed. I didn't say that I had seen it or knew about it personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. And another thing that I'd like to check out, on the basis of what you said yesterday: You have a pension of some kind, do you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't have a pension of any kind?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And were your years of service in the Bosnian Army counted for as years of service?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. He did have his service in the BH Army, was certified and confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, before we move on to 1995 and Srebrenica, let me just see one thing. Yesterday, I mentioned that I stopped the Republika Srpska Army at the borders of Srebrenica because we were afraid that the people would take their revenge, because 1.200 Serbs had been killed in that area and that was quite fresh in everybody's mind. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reason you say you stopped them from doing -- from things happening, well, what happened happened in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about 1993 now, and for that would you look at the four localities I'm going to show you now. But let me ask you this: Of those 1200 people killed, how many of them were killed in your village and the surrounding parts?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in my village?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you know that many people were killed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, quite a lot of people were killed. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask the usher to hand the witness this piece of paper with four localities on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't have to read the names out, but just tell me if they're places in and around your village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you have looked at the piece of paper -- have you? We don't have to display it. But can you see those four places?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are those four places around your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All those four names, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you wait? We are not able to see the document yet. ELMO hasn't been prepared. Let's wait and see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then we'll take a look at it directly. Could you bring it to the Bench. Very well. We can proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I'd like this piece of paper, under seal, to be admitted, those four localities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. What is the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D44, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd now like to have called up on e-court document 1D859, please. We have to be careful with the name on the photograph or that this photograph should not be displayed in public, the name of the locality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One way to do it is to roll down the document so that we can't see the name of the village. Yes, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very good, that's been solved, then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, are those victims from one of those localities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to have that admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This can't be broadcast, but we have passed already. And the number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D45, perhaps under seal because of the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you, Mr. Nicholls. I take it there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: There's no objection. And to be open, if we just write over the name, I have no objection to that either, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have 1D860 next, please. And may we proceed in the same manner as with the previous picture; that we scroll down so that the name of the locality cannot be seen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this tree?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that it's a willow tree or, rather, a tree for hanging Serbs from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who says that? Who says Serbs were hung from this? That is 100 per cent a lie. I saw a tree similar to this, and you slaughtered lambs, and we found the skins of lambs under one such tree. So that's a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We determined that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could have hung anything from that tree, just a pair of trousers or a shirt or whatever, but what you're saying is 100 per cent a lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have document 1D861, please, to show what was found on the tree. I'd like the Trial Chamber to see that and to see the locality, and then we can cover the locality up. 861 is the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, Karadzic, do you know where this place is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, the people who investigated know where it is.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But wait a minute. Is that the territory of a Serb village or a Bosniak village?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your village, there were Serbs and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you tell me, Mr. Karadzic. When those Serbs came, they expelled all the Bosniak people and set fire to all the houses. We had four mosques. All four mosques were destroyed by them. You set fire to three women, and they were burnt. You killed an old man of 80 who didn't want to leave his home. You're not saying that, you're not saying any of that. You're talking about three or four kilometres one way, and three or four kilometres another. There was no Serb village in the vicinity. Where did you expel all those people to, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is your village, in which you killed the Serbs from your village and captured Serbs who enjoyed the protection of the Geneva Conventions, and this has been established.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But we'll provide the court records of this in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this into evidence next. And may we have 861 displayed to show the situation that the Serb Army encountered when it entered the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, can I ask your position as to all of the pictures or photos that seems to be going to be presented?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my position would be that they're of extremely limited relevance, if any. The witness now just answered - I don't think he needs to take his headphones off - that he was asking which village this tree is in, and he didn't recognise it. So Mr. Karadzic has said that he will bring a witness, if I understood him right, who will discuss this investigation, and that might be a more appropriate way, somebody with first-hand knowledge who can go through these photos. But they are of very limited relevance, if any, although they are obviously disturbing to look at, if we go through each and every one of these.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 100 per cent sure, it's not true, sir, and that's 100 per cent sure. This is just a Serb fabrication. You know what Serbs can fabricate, no one else can. I don't know whether it's exactly this tree, but I was by a tree like this where they put a beam so that they could skin sheep and then roast them and eat them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we mark for identification all of these photos, and I don't see much point of putting each of them to the witness, who is not likely to confirm any of the photos. And then I think you have another opportunity to bring witnesses who can testify about photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. I would briefly like to show this. This is part of a court exhibit, and it actually had to do with proceedings related to the situation that the army found in his village when they entered it. The next photograph will show this, 862.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's try just three of them. Choose three pictures and then show -- photos, and then show them to the witness, and let's see what he can answer to those pictures.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Then 862, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are exhumations that were carried out by a judiciary organ. Actually, do you know that this exhumation was carried out on this hill?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know about that. But, yes, they were buried there. Yes, I know that. I had seen those few dead people, yes. As for the hanging, that is a 100 per cent lie. We were not taking people prisoner and hanging them, no. Somebody just invented that. What kind of nonsense is this? There is no law that can prove that there were any hangings. You exhumed these people after three months. You did not find them hanging. Don't tell us all this nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D642, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, it's all from yesterday, 28800 through to 83, and the page number is 15. It's from the Milosevic transcript. President Milosevic says to you, What did you use to kill all these Serbs? And your answer was, Rifles only. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to see whether you killed them with something else or whether you massacred them once they were dead.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who massacred who, I don't know. I cannot tell you about that. I cannot say yes or no. I just know -- let me tell you. Your soldiers brought a box of ammunition. They went to a small village consisting of, say, eight houses that they hadn't burned yet, and people were still living in these houses. When they went to that village, they actually missed it, and they went in the other direction. Perhaps it's about a kilometre away as the crow flies. People were shooting, and they hit the windshield of that small TAM truck, and then they took this wounded person and went back. When our people came, just before night they found a box of ammunition containing 5.000 bullets. I want to tell you about these bullets. They were killed with those bullets that they had brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, let us stick to --

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you denying that these people were exhumed there, and that at all four localities there were mass graves and they were exhumed? Are you denying that, or are you confirming that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that. I just know that that trench on the front-line that you held, people didn't want to dig that, and then that was covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, what is your position regarding Defence evidence 860 to which the witness seemed to have confirmed to a certain extent, an exhumation picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have it on the screen, but my recollection was that he didn't know anything about the exhumation, but that he'd heard or saw that people had been killed. Going back to the tree, the witness said he didn't know what that tree was or where it was, so I do not think that a foundation has been laid for those two to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me go back to his answer. After he said: "No, no, I don't know about that," he said: "But, yes, they were buried there. I know that." Lines 8 and 9, page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean, no objection, then. But he simply couldn't say this was a photo of that exhumation. He wasn't familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about 642, which was just shown, which is coming -- seems to be coming from the Milosevic trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the tree -- the photo of a tree, 640, it seems to be identical to one of these pictures, if you take a look at page 5 of this. But we'll see whether it's identical or not. So we mark for identification 640, and the number is ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be MFI D45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we admit 862 and 642.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D46 and D47, respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now please have 641, 641.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is a court record of the on-site investigation. It is the basic court Zvornik, and the date is the 22nd of February, 1993. It is a record of the on-site investigation, and it says that it is that first, second, third, and fourth locality that you confirmed was in your area. And it has to do with the exhumation and identification of members of Republika Srpska from common mass graves that were taken prisoner -- these people were taken prisoner at Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, they got killed at the front-line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a court record.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look, let me tell you. Ninety per cent and even more were people who were not from that territory at all. These were people from other areas, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move on to page 3 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have no English translation, do we?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. For the time being, there doesn't seem to be one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Person number 15, the corpse is deformed, the skull is crushed. There were traces of burning on the stomach, and skin is burned as well. It is the son of Bogdan - I'm not going to mention the name - born in 1949, from your village. He was identified by his wife. Sir, so there are four mass graves. In every one of them, there were mutilations. Heads were cut off, bodies were burned, roasted. Is that what you are denying?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that did not happen. There was one corpse without a head, but there was no one that had been burned or roasted. Perhaps some corpses were perhaps deformed because they were dragged somewhere, but I can guarantee that it wasn't more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is the transcript all right? Thank you. Let's not dwell on it any longer. You're going to get a translation of this. 641, could that please be admitted, together with 642, with all the other documents, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection to it being marked, Your Honour. But we don't have a translation. I'd like to see more, what is in this. And the witness has not read the document, does not know anything about this document, but it can be marked at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So 641 will be marked nor identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI D48, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And for the sake of time, we'll mark for identification all the other photos, pending until we hear the evidence from other witnesses. Mr. Karadzic, let's move on to your real topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us just finish with this briefly. Did the Serb Army show up for the first time in November 1992 in your area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That Serb Army threw us out. They were the ones who threw us out. They burned all our houses. I saw, with my very own eyes, how my own house was burning. I do not feel sorry for these people, even if they all got killed. Whoever comes to steal somebody's property or ruin someone's property and someone's home, may he not return to his own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's finish with that part, and let's move on to 1995. I'm going to tell you something, Mr. Witness. That Serb Army tolerated you and the fact that you were shooting at them, at the back, all the way up to November 1992.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They tolerated us, I don't know, from the 19th or 26th of April all the way up until that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, I would appreciate if the Court Officer would circulate to the parties the exhibit number of all the photos that have been marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, did your army close the road going across Konjevic Polje to Zvornik? Up until then, we couldn't use it at all.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did your army make incursions to Crni Vrh in order to close the road through Zepardi?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to wait for a moment. Is Crni Vrh close to you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly have this map put on the projector? It's a map of the international community. I think it's a NATO map, or UNPROFOR. I got it from the OTP, I think. Yes. Would you please put this part there, this part [indicates], so that we see this part. This can be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see this here? Between Srebrenica and your area, there is Serb territory, Serb-controlled territory. And, see, from here we can see how you get to Crni Vrh, and that is what is written here. May I remind you that you were attacking from there; not only the army, in the back, but you were also attacking civilian convoys, and you also killed a busload of civilians?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where, where? Crni Vrh?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crni Vrh is 70 kilometres away. I mean, how could somebody get there? They'd need a bus to get there. How can I get out of Srebrenica? I can only go to Potocari, Suceska. We were as if we were in a camp. We were just waiting to get killed by someone. Come on, how can you compare that, Srebrenica and Crni Vrh, I mean really truly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it were somewhere closer, all right, but Srebrenica and Crni Vrh, come off it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, Crni Vrh is near Zepardi. You see where this green, three-pronged line is.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Crni Vrh is 20 kilometres away from my village and at least 70 kilometres away from Srebrenica. And what did they take? Aeroplanes. What? I mean, from Srebrenica to do that? I mean, really and truly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, sir, from your village, before the fall of your village.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My village? We could not defend ourselves, we could not defend our village. Could we go and attack someone else further away?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to state something now.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goodness gracious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is an UNPROFOR map that shows that you are going to the Pale-Zvornik road near Zepardi and that you're threatening that road as well. You're already holding the one near Konjevic Polje, and you're threatening this one. And you killed not only soldiers there. I mean not you, personally, but your army. They killed civilians as well, including a bus full of civilians that got killed there. Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I just want to ask you what you have to say to this: If I tell you that the army could no longer tolerate your shooting in the back and your interruption of all roads --

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how about you telling me, Mr. Karadzic ? Did you attack all of Bosnia-Herzegovina? There is not a single place in Bosnia-Herzegovina that you did not attack. Take a map, have a look at it. Look, the Court is here, the Prosecutor is here, your Defence, everybody. In all of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you occupied territory. You attacked Sarajevo, Bihac, Zenica, Visoko, Olovo, Kladanj; that is to say -- oh, yes, Tuzla as well. There is not a single place that you did not attack. All right, if it were just in one place, but you were attacking all over the place. That was in your interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, part of the problem is the questioning. This is not a question: "Thank you, sir. I just want to ask you what you have to say to this: If I tell you that the army could no longer tolerate your shooting in the back and your shooting of all the roads." There needs to be a clear question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My understanding was to be that he was putting his case to the witness, and the witness denied it. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender the map into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, you said this is an UNPROFOR map, but the marking is done by you; am I correct in so understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It's an UNPROFOR map showing the situation as they monitored it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have the ERN number of this map, or the 65 ter number, or some kind of indication of what exactly it is we have on the screen, because that hasn't been put into the record and I haven't seen the map, other than this section we can see on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I don't see this document in his documents for cross-examination. Was it included in the list?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It was not, Your Honour. I did not object because I know that occasionally a map is -- but I don't know what we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the usher could hand over the map to Mr. Nicholls and so that he can examine it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it wasn't on the list, I'd like it marked for identification. They'll be many more such maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls is not opposing to this practice, so it's okay. But whether -- let's see whether Mr. Nicholls can confirm it or not. You can proceed while Mr. Nicholls is examining the map. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because my time is short, Witness, we have to -- or, rather, I will put things to you cumulatively. During your five testimonies and several statements and reports, so you testified five times, gave five statements and five reports, you gave fairly contradictory data when it comes to the details, and if we had time, I would go into all those details. But let me ask you this now: When did you leave your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left my village in 1993, sometime in February perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In some statements and testimonies, you say that it was in October 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They expelled us in 1992. The ones that you showed us pictures of a moment ago, they expelled us, but they set their fire -- houses on fire in October. And when they were killed, this was on the 6th of November. Those are those favourite people of yours who came to expel us and set fire to our houses, yes. That was in October. We moved out, but then we returned and lived in those half-burnt-down houses. When the women and children left, the Serbs came again, and we had to withdraw again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't accept this blanket statement about contradictory data being given. I asked yesterday in the future that sites be given, according to the Court's guide-lines, to statements. So if the cross-examination is now going to focus on statements made by the witness, I'd ask that the guide-lines be followed and we be given the reference whenever Mr. Karadzic is talking about a particular point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. That was in his testimony during the Tolimir trial. I'll find the reference. But if I'm to do that, then I'll need far more time, if I'm going to look into every contradictory piece of evidence that this witness provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't think that does require further time. I think that's an incredibly weak argument for a witness that the accused has known about since October, has had all the statements for a long time. And the Tolimir statement, as soon as it came out. It's a basic part of preparing your cross, that when you're going to put a statement to a witness, that you know where it comes from and that you are able to back that up. That shouldn't take a lot more time; that's just you prepare a cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. It's in the transcript, 513 [as interpreted] to 5873, pages 7 and 8, in the Tolimir trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just tell us very briefly, what did your trip to Srebrenica look like, what was it like?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we left our village, we arrived in Konjevic Polje and spent six days in a house there. And when Mr. Morillon arrived, Morillon went up to the Hrncica Mosque and raised a United Nations flag there. And we all left Konjevic Polje and withdrew upwards towards a place called Pervani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just give me the time. When was that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you. It might have been sometime around the 5th or 6th of March; when we were in Konjevic Polje, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how long were you in P ervani?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how many of you were there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I and my two brothers, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Weren't there any more people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. People were living in their houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So, sir, you didn't leave your village in a large group and reach Konjevic Polje and later Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were in a big group when the column set out towards Srebrenica. That's how we got to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said, sir, that there were several hundred of you; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There might have been several thousand, not hundreds. The people were on the move all the time. We just joined the column and set out with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when did you arrive in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was on the 13th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before that, your family had left for Tuzla. Why didn't you go to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go, and I explained yesterday why I didn't go. When we set out to Tuzla, all of us together, we were cut off, the column was cut off and the road was cut off, and we couldn't pass by that way. But we wanted to go to Tuzla before we were supposed to go to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, in Srebrenica, you tilled the soil of some Serb; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you lived in the town or the village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was the Serb whose farm you worked on?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how do I know? He was a refugee somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said here that Srebrenica had been demilitarised. Now, I'd like to tell you that not even the Prosecution claims that anymore and that the Secretary General of the United Nations informed the Security Council that Srebrenica and other protected areas were strongholds of the Muslim Army, military strongholds. And the Prosecution, in a pre-trial brief -- in its pre-trial brief, in paragraph 52, accepted the fact that Srebrenica was not a demilitarised zone, but that it was armed.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a rule, that secretary should be sitting on your side over there, and Yasushi Akashi should be on the other side, and then we should have a trial. The United Nations are the main cause of the deaths in Srebrenica. They disarmed the people and allowed the executioners to kill them all. Do you know, gentlemen, that you killed babies that had just been born several minutes ago, right up to old people who were 90 years old?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me. The question was whether Srebrenica was demilitarised. What is your answer to that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, it was demilitarised. But do you know, Mr. Karadzic, when the Canadian Battalion arrived, that you committed a great massacre in 1993, in the month of April, when over 60 inhabitants were killed, women, children, adults, in front of a school building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, we do not have much time, so please try to answer the question. Let's move on to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So the massacre that you mentioned, we have evidence and proof that we're going to present here was carried out by Naser Oric on orders from Sarajevo. But let's leave it there, because we're going to prove that in due course. Anyway, you were living in Srebrenica and you know what happened in Srebrenica. Was this gentleman Mr. Golic in Srebrenica whom you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is Golic is multiple murderer?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he is or isn't. I didn't socialise with Golic. I don't know, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who was the boss of Srebrenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, who? The people. Who else? Who would be the boss? There were no bosses. There were just poor people. I went without salt for months. And you can only be a boss if you have a lot of money.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, who was the main authority in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the head of the municipality was, and he's the same one that is the head now, when Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there a lot of mutual killings in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe the odd one, but I didn't see anybody kill anybody else in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And have you heard of Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you accept that he was killed by a group belonging to Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that, but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And were weapons brought in to Srebrenica during the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either. I'm small fry. I was a small fish in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's move on to 1995 straight away. That would be better, because there is a great deal of contradiction -- many contradictions that I'm going to submit to the Trial Chamber in an acceptable form in due course. Now, you said that you never heard or saw any fighting before the 11th of July around Srebrenica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, and there wasn't any fighting then either. The people left without any fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said, in the transcript of the 11th of March trial, 2010, T-513 to T-5873, page 519, I believe it is -- this is what you said: "Everybody decided to flee --" [In English] " ... on July the 11th, 1995. Nobody remained in Srebrenica. Nobody dared to remain, except handicapped people, which they, the Serbian forces, probably killed if they came across such handicapped people. Everybody else had to leave." [Interpretation] Now, Witness, did the Serb Army really kill somebody who was handicapped in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so. There was a man from my village. His son took him out. He might have been between the ages of 75 and 80. He wasn't an invalid, but he couldn't stand on his legs. And they said that they took him to in front of a building, and the Serb Army turned up that day. Now, the man wasn't transferred anywhere, so I assume he was destroyed, killed, straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you just tell me what you know about and not what you think?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no sign of him. He wasn't exchanged, so I assume that the first people who turned up killed him. Now, whether there was anybody else, I don't know. I know about this man. He stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, you very often say that you never saw somebody anymore. Does that mean that you know he was killed? He might have been sent home or transferred somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know his family, and his son was there. He lived next to me after the fall of Srebrenica as a refugee. His father never appeared anymore. One of his sons was in Tuzla, and that son who took him out of the house wasn't able to relocate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Nicholls said yesterday that your brother, who was handicapped, managed to reach a vehicle, to board a vehicle, and to go to Kladanj or Tuzla. Anyway, to cross over to Muslim territory. Now, did he manage to do that on his own or was he enabled that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was just lucky, because they separated the people to one side, and when his turn came, a soldier said to him -- he said, Get up onto the truck, whereas he had two crutches and said, I can't jump onto the truck. And then somebody else said, There's a bus for you, and he boarded the bus. And a Roma, a gypsy, said -- he said - Zarko, I think that's what his name was - they separated my son, and he said, Call them. And when the gypsy's son came by, another van came by too, and they managed to board the bus and were transported else somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, you said that everybody decide to do leave Srebrenica on the 11th. That's what you say in one place. And in another place, in the Popovic trial, transcript of the 25th and 6th of August - 742 is the page number - you say that somebody came and said, Now, people, we have to leave Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, nobody said that. The people decided what they were going to do amongst themselves. Nobody informed anybody of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what did the people decide?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, the people decided to take to the woods and go that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we have two groups of people. You're talking about the ones who decided to take to the woods and move towards Tuzla and fight. And what about the civilians who decided to go to the United Nations on the 11th?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, many people left, the women and children. It was only one woman who didn't manage to reach Potocari. But, anyway, the people in Potocari suffered the same fate as the others that took to the woods. Very few people managed to cross over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to know now who helped you, the civilians, to reach Potocari.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were vehicles, trucks from Srebrenica. I don't know whether it was UNPROFOR, but it was the trucks that were in Srebrenica. People who could walk walked, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can Mr. Karadzic check his cite, page 742, and let me know if he's talking about a different page of the transcript? The witness there does not say somebody came and told him to leave. He says: "We took the decision ourselves."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the citation, The Popovic case: "People, we've got to leave Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who is it that said that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that someone had said that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. No one said, People, we've got to leave Srebrenica. The people left the upper part of Srebrenica a day before. They all withdrew to the area where the hospital was. And from then on there was a lot of commotion. People didn't know what they wanted to do, and then they decided themselves, the people, to go through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're talking about the group that went with the army through the woods. First of all, let us establish now, when did people get to Potocari; how did they get there, and on whose decision?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People went to Potocari on the 11th of July. They all left Srebrenica on the 11th of July. They went to Potocari, and we went through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, did UNPROFOR help you? Did they help the people get to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know that when I was leaving Srebrenica, a shell fell near the UNPROFOR base, and that's when people jumped onto trucks. I think that they tore up the tarpaulin because they were so afraid. A man went with me. He parted from his daughter. His daughter stayed on, crying, and we set out through the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your handicapped brother, did he stay in Srebrenica, or did he go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He went to Potocari. A disabled man, who had only one arm, drove him to Potocari on a truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, you say that you gathered in Susnjari?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many people were there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, our estimate was that there were about 15.000 people there, perhaps a bit more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's your estimate; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many of them were armed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, I don't know. Maybe about 400 rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Rifles, how come? How come they had rifles all of a sudden?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I was from the third municipality. I really didn't know these people anyway. But it was so fortunate. Perhaps they had hidden those rifles. Those people who had rifles then managed to get through. Those who didn't have rifles are still lying in mass graves, or perhaps they're lying in Tuzla, in those bags, whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The journey through the woods, had it been organised?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, when you testified in Krstic, transcript page -- it's actually the 11th and 12th of April, 2000. The page reference is 2652. You said that the commanders knew about that, that the commanders had to know about that, about this decision to go through the woods?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. When we all gathered in Susnjari, of course this column set out and you couldn't even notice that they were leaving. Of course, these top people most probably -- well, I'm not saying. I left Susnjari with the last group. Now, did they agree how they left? I have no idea. There were too many people there. During the night, the column set out, and I left perhaps in the late afternoon hours on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A column was established in Susnjari; right? What date?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we arrived on the 11th, so approximately on the 11th, in the evening. That means that I left Susnjari on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many people were there in this column?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm telling you, no one could see how big the column was. It was being established non-stop, and people were leaving in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you went through the Buljin forest; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are some things that are unclear here. Where was your brother? At one point, you lost him, and then you found him again. What can you say about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were moving through Buljin, and then we could see everything. When night fell, I did not sleep. I didn't sleep that night. That night, in the evening, I lay underneath a birch tree and I slept there. When I got up at dawn, my brother was there. One group was moving forwards, the other group was moving backwards. I moved a bit back, and then I moved ahead again, and then I found my brother over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Popovic case, the 24th and 25th of August - the page number is 648 - you said that you found your brother and that you sat there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we sat there all day, practically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Throughout the 13th?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Later on, you say, in your statement or your interview before the investigating judge of the Higher Court in Tuzla on the 29th of July, 1995, page 5 -- this is what you say. It's translated into English: [In English] "The column was formed again and started going into the direction of Konjevic Polje, through the woods above Kamenica." [Interpretation] Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. When we set out towards Kamenica, that's when we decided to surrender. In the woods -- we were still in the woods. We did not see a single field until the Serbs called out to us, telling us that we had to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in Popovic, on the 25th, on page 643, you say something similar to what you're saying here now: "No, I don't even know --" [In English] "... No, I don't even know what Kamenica is. I only told you that we passed through a torched village, and we knew that was a Muslim village because it had been torched, and we were supposed to surrender there." [Interpretation] Is it correct that you don't know what Kamenica is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. To this day, I don't know where this village of Kamenice is. It's not Kamenica, it's Kamenice. It belongs to Konjevic Polje up there by Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that you saw some bodies of persons who were killed, and in the Popovic case - the transcript page is 843 - you say that you saw about 50 bodies by the road?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, in the Tolimir case, the transcript of the 11th of March, 2010, page 522 -- 513 up until 584, page 10 specifically, you said: [In English] "I could see many corpse of civilians in the woods to the right of the road where we were on. To the left, there was a slope, and so I did not see many corpses in that direction. I do not know how those people were killed. I saw a man lying in group of two or three, and some bodies were dismembered. I think there were more than 500 corpses in the woods."

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's not what I said, no. I didn't say that anybody had been massacred, no. I don't remember -- Tolimir didn't even ask me about that, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it is time for a break? I have to ask, how much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, I moved quickly through many things, through many inconsistencies that certainly bring into question a great deal of this testimony. However, now we are getting to a period that is full of all sorts of unbelievable stories, and I would hope at least for one more session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You spent more than four hours already. I would expect you to conclude in half an hour in the next session. Mr. Nicholls, are you in the position to answer the question as to the map, UNPROFOR map?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm not familiar with this map. I'm looking for it, as I can in the courtroom. I don't -- it doesn't have an ERN. I haven't seen this map. I will check during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we mark for identification for the time being?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the number is ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be D69, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And I have one further question to Mr. Nicholls, is whether you are following the page number Mr. Karadzic is referring to. I couldn't find the passages on the page he referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have not -- I have not been able to find the passages on the pages, and I was going to ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: During the break, could you liaise with Mr. Robinson and the accused to check this, to sort it out?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Twenty-five minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger. We have a new member.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're joined by Mr. Patrick Hayden. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Welcome, Mr. Patrick [sic]. Mr. Karadzic, let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before I start, I'd just like to give the references, the one that I gave at the last session. Popovic, the 25th of August, 2006, when they said: "People, people," that's what you say in our language, "we have to leave Srebrenica." That is 17 -- page 17. What is this? Oh, line 17. 814 is the page. The date is the 25th of August, 2006. Krstic is as follows: "Commanders had to know about it." 11th of April, 2000, line 5, page 2652.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go on, let's move on. My apologies, Mr. Hayden. I should hear Mr. Tieger out. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, a moment ago you said something that confused me, that there was no fighting and that some people had left even before the 11th, that is to say, on the 9th and 10th. Are you trying to say that Srebrenica was not defended, that it was abandoned?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was not defended? So the Serbs were simply allowed to walk in?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, as I said, your statements differ in many details, practically all of them, but I don't have time to deal with all of that. I'd like to put something to you. When you described your column, you said there was a column, and at the very rear there was a white vehicle of the United Nations. That is precisely what the column looked like, the one that consisted of civilians going to Kladanj. Sir, did you go to Kladanj or to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Who said that the column went with this white vehicle? The white vehicle could be seen in Divic, in front of the Vidikovac Hotel. No, no, I did not go to Kladanj. I went to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, no theft of a UN vehicle was registered at the time, and you said that there was this vehicle escorting you at the very rear of the column.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. The vehicle went to the very front. We saw the vehicle as we were moving from the quarry. We were moving towards Divic, from that tunnel. I saw that vehicle in the school-yard. It is 100 per cent certain that it had been taken away from UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I object to the comments, such as, There were many, many inconsistencies, but I won't have time to deal with them. That could have been any inconsistencies he finds, he should have dealt with. Again, we're not getting citations at all for this column. And it's not accurate, from any memory I have, what's been put to the witness. And, again, the last cite we got, as far as I can tell, was incorrect, and I want to put on the record that the representation of what was said in the Tolimir trial about 500 corpses is not -- in the woods, is not there either. So I'd ask for some care and precision in the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you understand, Mr. Karadzic? Then your general submission, for example, stating that there were many contradictions in general does not help the Chamber at all. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm prepared to provide this in writing to the Trial Chamber; what this relates to, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, you said that they were shouting. You said that -- you said they were shouting, saying, Take them to Alija, although you said "Halija." Serbs do not use the phoneme H as much as the Muslims do. We usually think that you use the H more than we do. Take them to Fikret and Halija, so they can be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that was when we spent the night in Bratunac, when they killed whoever they wanted to. For the most part, they were looking for people from well-known villages around Srebrenica. In the morning when at dawn, they said, Now take them either to Fikret or to Halija and have them exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vujadin Popovic, the transcript of the 24th and 25th of August, 2006. 668 is the page reference. Which Fikret did you mean?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They probably meant Fikret Abdic. I don't know what other Fikret they could have meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you know that at that point in time, Fikret Abdic and Alija Izetbegovic were sworn enemies, and Fikret Abdic was a Serb ally?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a Serb ally then. They probably meant Fikret Abdic. That's what I think. But they did not say that. They didn't say, Take them to Fikret Abdic and Alija Izetbegovic. They just said, Take them to Halija and Fikret.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is no other prominent Fikret; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There isn't? I don't know. I mean, there may be. Perhaps you know of one. I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, Witness, you said that there were some Arkan's men there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're the only person mentioning Arkan's men --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. For the Prosecution to be able to follow, you should give the page reference. Yes, Mr. Nicholls. Is that what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That was it, Your Honour. I was wondering where we are in the chronology of the witness's evidence. He just says, There were Arkan's men there. I believe there is a reference. I think I know where he's looking for, but I need the page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the transcript of the 11th of March, 2010, in the Tolimir trial. 526 is the page number. About Arkan's men.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you are the only person who could have envisaged Mladic and Arkan's men as being together on a territory covering 100 kilometres at that time in July 2005 [as interpreted]. There were no Arkan's men at that time.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where we were taken prisoner in the field, when they replaced each other, those who left said, These are Arkan's men. So the soldiers who were there first, and then were replaced by the others, said, These are Arkan's men. I didn't say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, again this is where we come back to the guide-lines which ought to be followed, which are not to paraphrase or summarise the witness's prior statement, but as much as possible to read back. Now, the witness has answered the question. But if you look at the citation, the witness did not say, These are -- it was put to him that he had said that Arkan's men were there. We don't know where "there" is because of the way the question is phrased, but in context it's at Sandici Meadow. That is not what the witness said in his prior testimony. What the witness said is that he was -- that another group was supposed to come, and this group of soldiers said something like, Well, here are Arkan's men. So the guide-lines would prohibit this type of changing the evidence, and, again, that these questions should be put precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree. Try to be precise in citing the previous testimony, Mr. Karadzic. And I take it that "2005" should read "1995." Let's move on. Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, the witness confirmed, when asked by me, that he said that, but I don't have time. But let me tell you. He said, Well, here are Arkan's men. And that is on the 11th of March, in the Tolimir trial, 2010, page 526. And then he said further on: [In English] "Later, this unit that guarded the prisoners was replaced by another unit of approximately 50 armed with automatic rifles, and the guards told us, before they left, that this unit consisted of Arkan troops. Witness in the breaks was not able to see their insignias. These other soldiers had the same camouflage battle dresses and the same type of equipment than those who left." [Interpretation] That, then, was stated in the witness's statement of the 14th and 15th of August, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you spent the whole day of the 13th in the woods; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you surrender?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I surrendered -- well, they gave us an ultimatum. The first ultimatum was in the 10.00. The second one was until after 4.00. We went to surrender. Now, how long that was, well, it was just before nightfall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what was the date of the surrender?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 13th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You think or you know?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the 13th, of course. We set out on the 12th, and on the 13th we surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did you surrender, what place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was around Sandici, that general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know who lives in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody lived there then. The Muslims used to live there, but at that time nobody was living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But aren't the Sandici a Serb village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it might be, but there are a lot of Muslims too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, I'd like to show the witness a document that we received last night, written by Mr. Naser Oric personally, in his own handwriting. I'll read it out first: "Conditions linked to Sandici. We cannot fulfill. We agree to an all-for-all change and an exchange without weapons; to the contrary, we won't feed your people, and we will act summarily." The commander of Srebrenica, and the date is the 10th of June. You see what happened to Sandici? Now, this phrase, "po kratkom postupku" or "summarily," what does it mean in our language?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 10th of June, 1992. But what does this phrase mean, when Oric means, We'll deal with your people summarily, we're not going to feed them? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Kravica came before Sandici. He couldn't reach Sandici through Kravica the way you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Witness, he had captured people?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a long way from Srebrenica. It belongs to Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Kravica belongs to Bratunac too, and Naser Oric attacked it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything belongs to everyone. If they attacked others, then those others attacked them, and that's quite normal. Now, Naser Oric would have been in 1992 what people were in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Just tell me, what does this phrase in our language mean, "summarily," "po kratkom postupku"?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that Mr. Naser Oric signed that, and I can guarantee that he had nothing to do with Sandici at that time. I can say that for certain, I guarantee that, because Naser Oric was incapacitated in 1992. He was under siege. If he could capture somebody, that's all he could do. He couldn't get a single bullet from anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that. I'm asking you what this phrase means in our language.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, whether to kill them or release them. But I don't believe that Naser Oric wrote this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you summarily execute someone or release them? Tell me that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know that best because you carried out those things summarily with Srebrenica in 1995. So you can -- you're the best placed to explain that phrase to the Trial Chamber here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We haven't got too much time, and everyone knows what "summarily" means. "Po kratkom postupku" means that execution is to take place summarily, summary execution.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, were we to blame for you to execute us? Were we to blame for anything? Were we guilty of anything? We were only guilty for having been expelled from our house because we were Bosniaks and not Serbs, and because that was your plan, to create an ethnic territory and to create a Greater Serbia, because your president, Slobodan Milosevic, always said, We want all the Serbs to live in a single state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is not a place where you are giving your evidence. You just put your question to the witness. Having heard the answer, you can ask another question, but do not put your statement. That is not helpful to the Chamber. How much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 10 minutes. I hope I'll be able to fit within the time-limit. I can't extend it, but I'd like to move on to another place, Grabovci or whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you say -- I can't find it now, but you say that you drove up-hill along that route.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Tell me where it says that. What road, what route, in what direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the whole night in Bratunac, and at dawn we left Bratunac. Now, when we set off from Bratunac towards Andagina Njiva, we went up the hill, and that's the only time that you could notice the column. You couldn't notice it anywhere else. I was in a trailer truck. So only when it goes uphill and downhill were you able to see anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, just a second. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
