utterances.text: Well, that's consistent with what I just said, that Dr. Karadzic was pointing out, at our initial meeting - this was the very first time we met in Belgrade - that the high birth-rate of the Muslims would enable them to achieve, as Dr. Karadzic said, their desires to have the whole of Bosnia to themselves, or to rule it, perhaps, by themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did Dr. Karadzic tell you at that same meeting, at least what he said the Muslims or Mr. Izetbegovic wanted to do with Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Karadzic took the position that Alija Izetbegovic, then the president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, wanted to turn Bosnia-Herzegovina into a Muslim -- Islamic state, with Sharia Law and all of the other appurtenances of Islam.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I just want to turn to one more reference in connection with that same matter. If we could turn to a meeting of September 17th, 1992. That's 65 ter 06535, page 26. And, Ambassador, that's ICFY book number 2, and it would be the sixth page of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And do we find there another reference to Dr. Karadzic's assertions that the Muslim birth-rate represented a threat to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Dr. Karadzic, in answer to a question from Secretary Vance, what of the current or the future situation, he responded that the Muslims were losing because their objectives were unrealistic, neither the Croats nor the Serbs would allow this, and that Izetbegovic is aiming at rule via a high birth rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the assertion that the Muslims were intending to rule via the high birth-rate and intended the establishment of an Islamic state, did Dr. Karadzic talk about other threats that he claimed that the Serbs had faced or were facing? For example, did he speak about any existential threats?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: Yes, in a broad sense, he did, because the constant references to the World War II genocide in Bosnia-Herzegovina against the Bosnian Serbs was a constant theme, and therefore that framed much of the discussion with Dr. Karadzic. It also had a geographic implication, because the Bosnian Serb official position with respect to their self-declared Republika Srpska was that areas that had had a Serb majority, a plurality, before the Second World War, where the Serbs were eliminated by a genocide, that those areas should revert to the Republika Srpska. So there was an existential aspect to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ambassador, you referred to the constant references to the -- to World War II genocide. Did the -- did you ever comment to Dr. Karadzic about the frequent repetition of this theme?

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: I don't know that I commented to him a great deal, but I do recall, early on, being somewhat shocked at these constant references. And I once said to him that if he continued with that line of thinking, that some day he'd commit a genocide himself, the Bosnian Serbs would commit a genocide. That was before the fighting began, actually. And I have to say that I didn't really take it seriously when I said it, except as a verbal way of expressing shock at the argumentation that World War II genocide justified all of Bosnian Serb behaviour. But it was noticeable. Also, in the note-books there's an entry which I did not mean to be humorous, but I noted a meeting with Dr. Karadzic, and at the beginning I wrote something to the effect -- it's in the journals, something to the effect that unusually Dr. Karadzic didn't mention Bosnian -- the genocide of the Serbs for three minutes into a conversation, because it was such a constant refrain with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I see the time, but I'll just refer quickly to 65 ter 06532, page 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Ambassador, that would be the Vance Mission book number 6 meeting at 2.45. I think it's marked page 104 in your diaries. It's actually on screen, Ambassador, if you can read that. A meeting at 2.45 to 3.25 of the -- of March 5th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that the meeting to which you just referred and the entry to which you just --

utterances.speaker: HERBERT OKUN
utterances.text: Yes. If I could just read the few lines. I wrote: "Summary: "Karadzic more disheveled and melodramatic, but did not use the word "genocide" until three minutes into the conversation."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ambassador.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ambassador, we'll adjourn for the day. We'll resume at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon. So I understand that you know full well that you're not supposed to speak about your evidence with anybody. Mr. Tieger, we went along without designating the exhibit number to the exhibit, but I hope that the Court Officer can convey all the numbers to the parties during the course of the morning tomorrow. So when we resume tomorrow afternoon, we are going to use the exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Rather than the 65 ter numbers. I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good evening, everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 23rd day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
